chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: The Garland bass players, Kid Ory's band and the New Orleans migration west
summary: They sort out which Garland played bass; Ed Garland of Kid Ory's band had just died, part of the New Orleans migration to Chicago and California.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. They had this man Garland playing the bass?
Yeah.
Which Garland was that?
I can't remember which one that was.
Was it Ed Garland?
No, Ed Garland was on the West Coast.
Is that the guy that was down here in New Orleans? Which of the Garland played basses down there? Supposed to be one of the oldest bass players around.
Oh, Garland on t the West Coast. Ninety-year-old Eddie Garland, worked with that band...
Ed Garland.
He just died.
Yeah, he died.

Barker - II-63

Those are the ones that migrated to Chicago, migrated from New Orleans around 1915, '16 and '17, and migrated from Chicago to Frisco and Oakland and San Diego. Jelly Roll and all of them went out there, when Watts was... They speak of Watts as a cowboy place, a country...you know, Western town.
That almost makes me the oldest one now standing. After you get past Garland and Pops Foster. I guess you ...(?)... and your day will come. There it is. You have to look at Bill Johnson...
